Traffic Advisory

The Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) led by the Honourable minister of the FCT Barrister Ezenwo Nyeson Wike CON is commencing yet another round of commissioning on Tuesday, 10th June 2025, starting with the newly rehabilitated International Conference Centre (ICC).

Hence there will be road traffic diversion away from ICC at the following points:

A) On Tafawa Belewa road,there will be diversion into Warri Street connecting Emeka Anyaoku street by First Generation Mortgage Bank,also in reverse direction as an alternative route.

B) The intersection on Herbert Macaulay way and Zakaria Maimalari street. Near National Defence College.

Motorists are advised to adhere to all diversion points as law enforcement personnel will be adequately deployed to guide movement.

Also to note is, standard protocols during the presidential movement will strictly be followed as the president is expected to attend the occasion.

Your usual cooperation is highly solicited. 

- Head Traffic, DRTS.

•Unauthorized immigrants often detained and deported
•Their constitution doesn’t allow foreigners to buy land near borders

🇸🇻 El Salvador
•Tight restrictions on non-citizens
•Deportation is common
•No path to legal residency without financial means or close family

🇬🇹 Guatemala
•Immigration violations treated as criminal acts
•Immigration status must be proven on demand
•Protesters in the U.S. often claim asylum while Guatemala offers almost no asylum

🇨🇳 China
•Zero tolerance for illegal immigration
•Harsh penalties, including prison and deportation
•Even legal immigrants face surveillance and employment restrictions

🇵🇭 Philippines
•Illegal immigration = arrest & deportation
•Foreigners can’t own land or stay beyond a short visa
•Some Filipino nationals protest U.S. enforcement despite their own strict national laws

🇳🇮 Nicaragua
•Highly restrictive immigration policy
•Prison for those who overstay or enter illegally
•Border security is strict under the Ortega regime

These countries enforce their borders to protect their people and resources. But when the United States tries to do the same?

“Racist.”
“Fascist.”
“White nationalist.”

It’s not about fairness—it’s about control through manipulation. You’re not crazy for noticing.

Today, June 9, 2025, has seen several significant and concerning events around the world. Here's a summary of some of the most impactful:
Natural Disasters and Environmental Concerns:
Tropical Cyclone Barbara (Mexico): A tropical cyclone named Barbara is impacting Mexico.
Flooding (Philippines): Heavy rainfall has been causing significant flooding in the southern Philippines, particularly on the western Mindanao island, leading to displacement and damage.
Earthquake (Colombia): An earthquake of magnitude 6.3 occurred in Colombia on June 8th, with its impact being assessed today.
Volcanic Activity (Guatemala): The Fuego volcano in Guatemala has seen increased humanitarian impact from its eruption on June 6th.
Severe Frost & Crop Losses (Turkey and other regions): A severe frost in Turkey has devastated apricot crops, with Malatya Province, a major producer, suffering catastrophic losses. This is expected to disrupt the global apricot market for over a year and impact prices. Other regions like Moldova, Bulgaria, Greece, Ghana (cashews), Pennsylvania (potatoes), and parts of Australia (fruits and vegetables) have also experienced significant crop losses due to extreme weather.
Wildfires: Certain regions are experiencing dramatic surges in wildfires, including recent fires in New Jersey's Pinelands.
Humanitarian Crises and Public Health:
Mpox Public Health Emergency: The World Health Organization (WHO) has reaffirmed that the mpox outbreak remains a public health emergency of international concern, citing a continuing rise in cases and likely undetected transmission.
Humanitarian Crisis (DRC): The conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has led to a sharp increase in rape and sexual violence against women and girls, with over 67,000 cases reported in the first four months of 2025 alone. Access to vital medical supplies like PEP kits is severely limited.
Sudan Emergency (Chad): The UNHCR is reporting on the ongoing Sudan Emergency situation and its impact on Chad.
Other Incidents:
Train Accident (Mumbai, India): Four commuters were killed and nine injured after falling from a crowded local train near Mumbra railway station in Mumbai.
Traffic Collision (Malaysia): At least 15 people were killed and 33 injured in a traffic collision in Malaysia when a bus crashed into a minivan.
Shooting (Las Vegas, USA): Two people were killed in a shooting at the Fountains of Bellagio in Las Vegas, Nevada.
Qantas Emergency Landing (Baku): A Qantas A380 flight from London to Singapore made an emergency landing in Baku, Azerbaijan, due to a passenger experiencing a sudden health deterioration.
It's important to note that information on global events can evolve quickly, and this summary reflects the most significant "catastrophic" events reported today, June 9, 2025.
